skill.name: convex-self-heal
skill.description: Production error → triaged, root-caused, repaired, and certified (tsc + rehearsal + reproduce-then-gone) fix PR for a human to merge — then confirm the error stops recurring. Never auto-merges.
skill.summary: Investigate Convex production errors, prepare certified fixes, and preserve human control over merging and deployment.
skill.author: get-convex

content.value_statement: Production errors often produce uncertain fixes that stop before verification. This skill triages defects, prepares certified changes, and keeps merging under human control.
actual_capabilities: Classifies Convex production errors as transient, configuration-related, or code and schema defects.
Uses sentinel data and Convex analysis tools to identify root causes with supporting evidence.
Prepares fixes on a branch or preview while preserving a mandatory human merge decision.
Certifies applicable changes with TypeScript checks, migration rehearsal, error replay, and regression checks.
Verifies after deployment that the original error signature no longer recurs.
Defers destructive, ambiguous, or unapproved changes for explicit human direction.
limitations: Requires sentinel capture and related Convex capabilities to be installed and available.
Does not merge pull requests or deploy production changes without human action and deployment consent.
Stops when the root cause is unclear or when applicable certification checks fail.
Production snapshots and error evidence require separate privacy, retention, and access controls.

use_cases.title: Triage a recurring production error
use_cases.description: Classify a recurring Convex failure, identify its cause, and decide whether a repair should proceed.

use_cases.title: Prepare a certified fix
use_cases.description: Create a reviewable branch and pull request with relevant checks, replay evidence, and a reversibility note.

use_cases.title: Govern automated remediation
use_cases.description: Define approved fix classes, preserve deployment consent, and maintain an auditable record of every action.

prompt_templates.title: Classify one production error
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Convex error: {error summary}. Classify it as transient, configuration-related, or a code or schema defect. Explain the evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage of a single error

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a recurring failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this recurring Convex error signature: {signature}. Use available sentinel evidence and analysis tools. Stop if the root cause remains unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare and certify a repair
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a branch-based fix for {confirmed defect}. Run every applicable certification check and produce review evidence. Do not merge or deploy.

prompt_templates.title: Run the governed healing workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Handle {incident} using the full gated workflow. Respect approved fix classes, sanitize production evidence, prepare a pull request, and verify after authorized deployment.

output_examples.input: A Convex function failed once because an external service timed out.
output_examples.output: Classification: transient. Retry or monitor the event, but do not open a repair pull request for this isolated failure.

output_examples.input: A recurring mutation fails because its validator rejects an expected field.
output: Root cause confirmed from recurring error evidence and the implicated mutation.
A validator fix was prepared on a branch.
TypeScript checks and replay verification passed.
A human-reviewed pull request is ready; no merge or deployment occurred.

output_examples.input: A schema change passes locally but fails against production-shaped records.
output_examples.output: Certification failed during migration rehearsal. The change was not proposed, and the incompatible record shape was reported for human review.

best_practices: Define approved fix classes and deployment consent before starting the workflow.
Redact and minimize production-derived data before using it in previews, findings, or pull requests.
Require every applicable certification check and verify the error signature after deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not prepare a fix when the root cause is uncertain.
Do not edit production directly, auto-merge changes, or bypass deployment consent.
Do not include raw secrets, personal data, or unnecessary production records in development artifacts.

faq.question: Does this skill merge fixes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It prepares and certifies a branch or pull request, but a human must review and merge it.

faq.question: What errors can enter the repair workflow?
faq.answer: Confirmed code or schema defects can proceed. Transient failures and configuration issues follow separate handling paths.

faq.question: What happens when the root cause is unclear?
faq.answer: The workflow stops and reports the available evidence. It does not prepare an uncertain fix.

faq.question: How are fixes certified?
faq.answer: Applicable checks include TypeScript validation, migration rehearsal, error replay, and confirmation that no new finding appears.

faq.question: Can it make destructive changes?
faq.answer: Destructive, ambiguous, or unapproved changes are deferred for explicit human direction.

faq.question: How does it confirm recovery?
faq.answer: After an authorized deployment, it checks sentinel data and logs for recurrence of the original error signature.
